lead.headline: Delhi's air turns severe after Diwali as monitors go dark, and the BJP blames Punjab's worst day of farm fires this season
lead.short: Delhi's Air Quality Index stood at 373 at 11.05pm on Sunday, with readings above 400 in Alipur, Bawana, Burari, Chandni Chowk, Mundka, Punjabi Bagh, Rohini and Vivek Vihar after Diwali fireworks. Several monitoring stations stopped showing real-time data as levels rose, and Congress and AAP accused the BJP government of suppressing air-quality figures.

why.text: Delhi's smog season has arrived on schedule, and the fight is now over whose data to trust and whose farms to blame.

more: Punjab recorded 1,152 farm fires on Deepavali, its sharpest single-day rise of the season, taking the state's total from 3,307 on 7 November to 4,459, official data show. Tarn Taran has the most this season, at 654. Delhi minister Kapil Mishra accused AAP leaders of "orchestrating" the fires and said an investigation could even lead to Arvind Kejriwal's arrest.

The stations that stopped reporting included RK Puram, Nehru Nagar, Mundka, Sonia Vihar and Dwarka, IANS reported. BJP MP Praveen Khandelwal accused the opposition of raising pollution only during Hindu festivals, and the BJP said the opposition had failed to fix the problem in 25 years in power.

update.new: Diwali night pushes Delhi into the severe range and starts a row over data and Punjab's fires.
update.front: Delhi's smog has become a fight over missing data and Punjab's farm fires.

seconds.headline: Nvidia's board opens an independent investigation after Jensen Huang tells staff of an affair with a suspected Chinese spy
seconds.short: Nvidia's board said on Sunday it was launching an independent investigation after chief executive Jensen Huang told staff he had been unfaithful to his wife. US officials believe the woman, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, was feeding information to Beijing. The board said it saw no sign that national security or company secrets had been compromised.

why.text: Nvidia sits at the centre of the AI economy, and doubt over its founder's future reaches every company that depends on its chips.

more: China's embassy in Washington called the allegations "groundless smears and slanders" in late October, and no one has been charged. US intelligence officials reportedly briefed President Donald Trump about their concerns a year ago, and senior administration officials told The New York Times they doubt Huang could have stayed unaware of her role all that time.

Jeffrey Sonnenfeld of the Yale School of Management, whose CEO summits have hosted Huang, told TechCrunch he put Huang's chances of keeping his job at "about a 50-50", while calling his career salvageable. Nvidia's shares slid on the news. "I'm responsible for an entire industry," Huang recently told Bloomberg.

facts.investigation: independent, announced by the board on Sunday

update.new: The board opens an investigation after Huang admits the affair to staff.
update.front: Nvidia's board is now investigating its own founder.

seconds.headline: Alcaraz beats Shelton 7-6, 7-5 to win his first Paris Masters and avenge his US Open defeat
seconds.short: Carlos Alcaraz won his first Paris Masters on Sunday, beating Ben Shelton 7-6 (5), 7-5 in an hour and 57 minutes and sealing it with a backhand pass on his second match point. It was his first Masters 1000 title of the season, and it avenged his US Open quarter-final defeat by the American in September.

why.text: He goes to the ATP Finals in Turin with back-to-back indoor titles after a season broken up by a wrist injury.

more: Shelton had the better of most of the first set. Alcaraz was erratic on the forehand, with six unforced errors in his first 24 points, and saved six break points before winning the tie-break from 4-3 down. He dropped serve early in the second set and broke straight back.

A wrist injury kept the Spaniard off the tour for four and a half months, and he missed Roland-Garros and Wimbledon. He had fallen short this year in Indian Wells, Miami, Monte-Carlo and Shanghai, and had never gone past the quarter-finals in Paris before this week. He won in Vienna a week ago. The ATP Finals start in Turin on 15 November.

facts.titles: Vienna and Paris in consecutive weeks

update.front: Alcaraz is the Paris champion, a week before Turin.

seconds.headline: A Houthi strike hits Riyadh's Aramco Tower, and footage shows more damage than the 'minor' harm Saudi Arabia admits
seconds.short: The Aramco Tower in Riyadh's central financial district was hit in a Houthi air attack on Saturday. Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said it suffered only "minor damage" and no one was hurt, but footage verified by the BBC shows at least one floor badly hit and windows shattered on more than one level.

why.text: A strike on the heart of the Saudi capital widens the war around Iran and keeps a risk premium on oil.

more: The Houthis said they also targeted Riyadh's airport and Aramco oil storage, and Saudi Arabia said its air defences intercepted and destroyed several missiles. A Houthi statement on the Saba news agency confirmed an attack on Riyadh's business zone without naming the tower.

It came a day after the Houthis accused a Saudi-led coalition of killing at least 33 people, including women and children, in an air strike on al-Shariyah, east of Sanaa; Saba said 39 were injured, and Saudi Arabia has not commented. An informal ceasefire collapsed in July when the Tehran-backed group declared a "maritime embargo" on Saudi Arabia.

facts.damage: Saudi Arabia says minor; BBC Verify footage shows a floor badly hit
facts.al-Shariyah strike: at least 33 dead, the Houthis say

stories.headline: Karnataka finds petrol with up to 31.2% ethanol against a 20% limit, and Kerala starts testing its pumps
stories.short: Tests on petrol from 67 locations in Karnataka found ethanol far above the prescribed 20% in fuel sold by several major oil companies, in some cases as high as 31.2%. Kerala's food and civil supplies minister Anoop Jacob on Monday announced random checks at fuel outlets in Thiruvananthapuram, Ernakulam, Kozhikode and Kannur.

why.text: Drivers' complaints about E20 petrol now have state lab results behind them, and other states may start their own tests.

more: Karnataka chief minister D.K. Shivakumar said inspections covered petrol pumps as well as the stages of ethanol blending and distribution. In Thiruvananthapuram, samples are being collected from two pumps and sent to a lab accredited by the National Accreditation Board for Testing and Calibration Laboratories, district supply officer Smitha S.R. said.

The Karnataka results raise questions about how transparent the blending of petrol sold across the country is. Kerala's civil supplies commissioner and taluk supply officers can inspect pumps and take legal action under a 2014 state notification. Union minister Suresh Gopi has defended E20 petrol, saying Karnataka and Kerala are free to conduct their own studies.

briefs.headline: Six of a family die in a Diwali-night fire at a crockery shop in Madhya Pradesh's Katni district
briefs.text: Six died in Barhi town: shopkeeper Puran Agarwal, 77, his wife Chandrakala, 74, his daughter-in-law and three grandchildren, the youngest two months old. Two people escaped; stored crockery fed the blaze, the collector said.

briefs.headline: A 10-year-old boy dies in Delhi's Narela when a skyrocket hits him in the chest, and his family blames the hospital
briefs.text: Rishi, 10, was bursting crackers with his family on Sunday night. His brother says doctors "walked slowly". Delhi's fire service took 214 fire-related calls on Diwali, 24 of them from firecrackers.

stories.headline: Sheikh Hasina asks Bangladesh for a new passport and ID card so she can return from India in December
stories.byline: THE TIMES OF INDIA · REUTERS · 9 NOV
stories.short: Former Bangladesh prime minister Sheikh Hasina has formally asked for a new passport and national identity card, Reuters reported, a step towards her planned return from India in December. Her lawyers at London's Matrix Chambers wrote on Monday to Preeti Rahman, the acting high commissioner at Bangladesh's mission in Delhi, citing the reported cancellation of her documents.

why.text: Her return would test Bangladesh's fragile politics and India's position as her host for more than two years.

more: "I respectfully request that you take the necessary steps to issue a new Bangladeshi passport and National Identity Card for our client," the lawyers wrote. They asked for the applications to be processed "expeditiously", citing her nationality and Bangladesh's "obligations arising under international human rights instruments".

Reuters called the request the clearest sign yet that Hasina means to act on her stated plan to return, more than two years after a deadly uprising forced her from power. She intends to surrender before a court. Her Awami League party remains banned in Bangladesh, and her return could reignite political and legal tensions.

facts.asked for: new passport and national identity card
facts.letter to: acting high commissioner Preeti Rahman, Delhi

briefs.headline: The Krakow gunman dies in hospital, and police confirm he had also killed his parents and sister
briefs.text: The 24-year-old died early on Monday; police shot him within three minutes of the attack starting. The six killed in the square were four Poles, a Briton and an Austrian woman. His father, 53, mother, 52, and sister, 21, were found at home.

update.new: The gunman died; his parents and sister were found dead at home.

stories.headline: The Sensex gives up an early rise as investors take profits after a seven-session rally, and the rupee breaks below 94
stories.byline: MONEYCONTROL · THE TIMES OF INDIA · 9 NOV
stories.short: The Sensex was down 0.44% at 80,641.73 at about 1.30pm on Monday after rising 340 points to 81,339.41 in early trade, as investors took profits from a gain of about 10.5% over seven sessions, the longest winning run this year. The rupee rose 24 paise to 93.74 a dollar in early trade, breaking below 94.

why.text: The rally ran on falling oil and foreign money, and both now depend on the Iran talks holding.

more: The Nifty fell 0.45% to 24,874.55 after touching 25,084.05, and the Nifty Smallcap 100 and Midcap 100 slipped about 0.1%. The rally that ended on Friday was driven by strong foreign fund inflows, easing crude prices and money leaving the global AI trade, Moneycontrol reported.

The rupee closed on Friday at 93.98, up 43 paise. Brent crude, which had climbed to about $117.64, is now near $98, helped by Donald Trump's weekend remark that further strikes on Iran were highly unlikely if negotiations progressed. "The improvement in diplomatic expectations is already reflecting in energy prices," said Amit Pabari of CR Forex Advisors.

update.new: Profit booking after the rally; the rupee breaks below 94.

briefs.text: Administrator Jared Isaacman said the missions "will demand technical excellence, sound judgment, teamwork, and courage". NASA has 32 active astronauts in its corps.

briefs.text: Enzo Le Fée scored the 1-0 winner from the spot after Brian Brobbey won a 36th-minute penalty. Chelsea, again without a recognised striker, changed shape once more, using a three-man midfield for the first time this season.

briefs.text: The 3-1 defeat left Palace bottom for the first time since December 2017, after four straight league defeats. They have two wins from 10 games and the league's worst defence, with 24 goals conceded.

briefs.headline: Anuj Shrivatri, 22, becomes India's 100th grandmaster and the first from Madhya Pradesh
briefs.text: The 22-year-old became India's 100th grandmaster by winning the ASEAN+ Individual Open in Ozamiz City, the Philippines, with seven points from nine rounds after losing his first game. Viswanathan Anand was India's first, in 1988.

briefs.headline: Barcelona win 2-1 at Atlético with two goals from Fermín López and stay three points clear of Real Madrid
briefs.text: Fermín López scored twice in the 2-1 win after Giuliano Simeone put Atlético ahead, ending a fortnight in which Barcelona lost to Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid. They are three points clear of Madrid.

briefs.text: Warner called Khawaja's revelations about the 2018 ball-tampering "100% accurate": "Uzzy wrote down every single thing from that day on." Cricket Australia says it remains "comfortable with the findings" of its integrity process.

stories.headline: All seven bodies in the Rajajinagar family murders are recovered, the last two from Shiradi Ghat
stories.short: Police have recovered all seven bodies in the murder of a Rajajinagar family, The Hindu reports, with the last two found in Shiradi Ghat. On Sunday police found two bodies near the foothills of Chamundi Hills in Mysuru, believed to be those of Shivakumar and Divya, the brother-in-law and sister-in-law of the accused, Indushekhar.

why.text: The case has shown how one man moved bodies across state borders without a single checkpoint stopping him.

more: Police recovered the Mysuru bodies with the accused present and drew up a spot mahazar. On Saturday they found the bodies of his wife, Sunita, and mother-in-law, Rupavathi, in a forest in Salem, Tamil Nadu, and a young boy's body had been found earlier near the foothills of Nandi Hills. A special team was sent to Shiradi Ghat for the last two.

An autopsy indicates fatal haemorrhage, The Hindu reported. Neither a patrol vehicle nor a checkpoint stopped Indushekhar as he crossed state borders with the bodies, the paper found. Police had traced five bodies by Sunday before the Shiradi Ghat search found the last two.

update.new: All seven bodies have now been found.

briefs.headline: Bengaluru's waste marshals book 68 cases and collect ₹76,500 in fines in a Sunday drive against dumping
briefs.text: BSWML marshals booked 68 cases and collected ₹76,500 on day and night patrols on Sunday, targeting garbage dumping, single-use plastic and footpath encroachments, the Greater Bengaluru Authority said.

stories.headline: Norris wins in Brazil as Verstappen charges from 21st to second, and Red Bull says he is beating the simulator
stories.short: Lando Norris won the Brazilian Grand Prix at Interlagos on Sunday, 14.6 seconds ahead of Max Verstappen, who started 21st after an engine penalty. Isack Hadjar made it two Red Bulls on the podium, ahead of George Russell and champion Kimi Antonelli. "No sim in the world will predict that you will go from P21 to P2," said Laurent Mekies.

why.text: The drive keeps Verstappen second in the standings, with three races left in a close fight for runner-up.

more: Mekies, Red Bull's team principal, said no simulation could predict "that you get 14 places in five laps". "He's beating the sim on a regular basis," he said. The penalty was not planned: "We had a small issue on Friday that forced us to do so." This is the first season of Red Bull's own power unit, built with Ford.

Verstappen had warned after qualifying that overtaking at São Paulo would be harder than in previous years. He is second in the drivers' standings on 279 points, ahead of Russell on 262, Lewis Hamilton on 261 and Charles Leclerc on 249. The Las Vegas Grand Prix follows at 09:30 IST on Sunday 22 November.

data.max_note: Drove from 21st on the grid to second in Brazil after an unplanned engine penalty.

briefs.headline: Jharkhand police seize 441 kg of ganja worth ₹2.2 crore and arrest four, most of it from a truck in Garhwa
briefs.text: Police found 426 kg in one-kilo packets hidden in a secret chamber of a container truck near Garhwa's Kalyanpur overbridge on Sunday. Four people were arrested in separate operations; in all, 441 kg worth ₹2.2 crore was seized.

briefs.headline: Four devotees die and 12 are hurt when a tractor-trolley overturns in Chitrakoot, and five are sent to Prayagraj
briefs.text: Most on board were from Prayagraj and Rewa, returning from the Diwali fair. The trolley's hook came loose near Ramnagar on the Jhansi-Mirzapur highway; four died, 12 were hurt and five were referred to Prayagraj.
